hook: SCP-3774 opens as a dry spec sheet for a surveillance project and then hands most of its length over to a run of recordings. Go in expecting a romantic comedy told through a very small camera, and let the tone shift on you as it goes. The ending is bodily and strange, involves reproduction, and the file stays matter-of-fact about it to the last line.
whyItMatters: Rather than threat or containment, the article is about a relationship told almost entirely in dialogue, which shows how far the clinical SCP format can stretch toward a love story. The project's flaw is a single, oddly human glitch, and the article treats it as both a joke and the engine of real feeling. The Neutralized class sits right at the top, so you read the whole romance already knowing it is over.
thingsToNotice:
The voice gives the truth away long before the reveal: 2432 claims to be a ghost, then a spy working remotely through microscopic drones, while the camera angles from the bookshelf and the windowsill keep reminding you how small she is. Merle, an elementary school janitor, names her Leslie because she sounds like Leslie Caron, and they grow close watching Eponine die in Les Miserables, which 2432 admires as love given without being returned.

The line about two weeks spent finding him and one week left to live turns the comedy into a countdown, and proving she is a mosquito means biting him, with a second bite standing in for a kiss. The last log is audio only as she fades, and her final idea is to lay eggs in him so he will have their kids. Three days later he is found with a mass in his thigh that turns out to be four human fetuses sharing half their genetic makeup with the mosquitoes; the Foundation alters his memories, gives him a new identity and moves the family to West Virginia to watch the children grow.
